summary.headline: PB Fintech Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose 37% for FY26 to ₹6,794 Cr; Q4 premium ₹29,934 Cr (+42% YoY) and PAT ₹670 Cr.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed accelerating insurance premium growth, with new insurance premium up 59% YoY net of savings and savings back to growth. Health remained the fastest-growing protection line and term was catching up. Paisabazaar turned EBITDA-positive on an operating basis but at a very small level, and management guided to significant positive EBITDA next year. Management said there was no board-level plan for the balance sheet beyond buyback/dividend discussion, and that PB Health may seek capital with PB Fintech having a pro-rata right only.

segments.name: Policybazaar core insurance
segments.commentary: Core online insurance premium up 39% for FY26 and 44% in Q4; new insurance premium up 59% YoY net of savings and 48% including savings. Health growing about 60%+ for 13 quarters.

segments.name: Paisabazaar (lending)
segments.commentary: Credit revenue up 7% YoY and disbursal up 11% YoY; wholesale POSP home-loan business stopped in January, and management said it was not material to profit. Operating EBITDA positive in Q4 but minuscule.

segments.name: PB Connect (home loan POSP)
segments.commentary: Wholesale business stopped, reducing revenue; management said it was losing about ₹0.5 Cr a month, so profit impact is nil.

segments.name: PB Corporate (employee benefits broker)
segments.commentary: Corporate business grew about 140% in Q4; management said it makes a small loss and will need investment, and it is in the top 8 brokers.

segments.name: UAE business
segments.commentary: Grew 54% YoY for FY; management said March was hit by the Gulf conflict but the business grew 3% YoY in March and about 10-12% in Q4.

guidance_outlook: Steady-state insurance premium growth: management said it always guides about 30% and beats that.
Paisabazaar: management expects operating leverage in FY27, with costs roughly flat and significantly positive EBITDA next year.
POSP to be pushed aggressively in FY27, with management expecting meaningful growth improvement next financial year rather than focusing on quarterly contribution margin.
Renewal revenue from Paisabazaar expected to be meaningful not in the next two years; company moving to upfront payments.
No new growth opportunity or acquisition under consideration in the last three months, per management.
Health insurance take rate: management said the insurance business has about 20% profit cushion versus industry, which it expects to retain through some mechanism.
capex_capacity: PB Health: one operating hospital in Noida (about ₹150 Cr revenue, ₹20-30 Cr profit); next hospital in Central Gurugram expected operational by end of May 2026; more hospitals being evaluated in Gurgaon and Delhi.
PB Care+ preferred network about 500 hospitals; plan to operate 500-600 network hospitals under PB Health brand over the next year.
Physical (phygital) fulfilment in 250+ cities, about 25% of savings, term and health business; management said the percentage grows only slightly each quarter.
Paisabazaar: no new employee additions for some time; management sees about 30% productivity leverage from the current employee base.
PB Fintech has a pro-rata right in PB Health (26-28% shareholding); PB Health is in late-stage talks to raise capital but has not approached PB Fintech.
demand_pricing: Health growth drivers: modular products, superior claims experience, and higher sum insured after GST; some insurers launched unlimited sum-insured products around ₹25 lakh; management said policies at ₹10 lakh and above are now the majority.
Term: premiums unchanged while customers saw an 18% reduction, leading to more rider attachment (critical illness and accidental riders); conversion rates have risen.
Savings: management said ULIPs carry the lowest take rates in the business; ULIP persistency about 70-75% after 5 years.
POSP: 99.5% of agents earn under about ₹20 lakh a year from PB; small agents now give 83% of POSP premium versus about 50-50 a year ago.
Paisabazaar: about 5.8 Cr consumers acquired to date; supplier base stabilised, with more larger partners added; conversion improved.

Commission/take-rate regulation: management said it has only heard about proposals from the media, with no regulator communication; it welcomes deferred commission and lower EOM structures in health and life.

qa_highlights.question: What drives new insurance premium growth (59% YoY) and what is steady-state growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are modular products, claims experience and a Q4 bump after GST; management said it always guides about 30% and beats it.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI quantify margin benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focused on sales-team productivity and customer experience rather than margin; the biggest use case is in claims and risk, not cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is PB Fintech investing in PB Health's next round?
qa_highlights.answer: No board or management discussion on new opportunities in the last 3 months; PB Health has not approached PB Fintech, which has a pro-rata right only.

qa_highlights.question: Paisabazaar margin and take-rate pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed costs have stabilised around ₹200 Cr and operating leverage should come in FY27; renewal revenue is becoming less important.

qa_highlights.question: Impact if take rates fall 50-100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the insurance book is about 20% more profitable than industry and the gain will be shared fairly; no speculation on specific mechanisms.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and PB Health update?
qa_highlights.answer: Only buyback and dividend discussion at management level; no plan yet; PB Health has used under 30% of its cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did new initiatives contribution margin fall to 4.3% from 5.7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is the same, reflecting mix shifts; 12-month rolling numbers should be used.

risks_watch: Regulatory risk: management says media reports on commission caps and deferred commissions have no regulator confirmation; any change could affect distribution economics.
Paisabazaar take-rate compression from credit card issuance and unsecured lending pressure; management did not split Paisabazaar's margin.
Quality of physical and POSP sales; management tracks claim settlement, loss ratio, persistency and renewal rates.
Term growth could slow as the comparison base changes; management says term will be challenging in the new year.
Receivables from insurers: management said the amount of revenue recognised but not yet received is not large, but gave no figure.
PB Health capital raise and the possibility of PB Fintech investing its pro-rata share.
summary.management_tone: Confident on insurance growth and claims-led positioning, with specific numbers given. Evasive on regulatory commission talk, Paisabazaar segment margins, term and health growth splits, and future capital allocation, which it said had no concrete plan.
key_quotes: We always guide about 30%, we always beat that guidance.
The main thing now is that we must continue to drive fresh growth, bring new customers to the insurance industry, and service them well.
We are no longer just a redirection platform, we are increasingly an end-to-end platform.
I think in bad times we'll perform okay; in great times, we'll really shine.
We have decided to stop the wholesale business, and it's a decision that we've taken, because we don't see any strategic value of that business.

adds.what: PB Health next hospital in Central Gurugram (operational by end of May 2026)
PB Care+ network expansion to 500-600 network hospitals under PB Health brand over next year

growth.why: Management says it always guides about 30% premium growth and beats it; FY26 revenue grew 37% and Q4 premium rose 42%, backed mainly by demand, health product mix and a Gurugram hospital coming online, while Paisabazaar guides roughly flat costs and significantly positive EBITDA next year with no hard capacity numbers.
